title: Boba Bhai revenue and losses jump over two-fold in FY26
summary:
Bengaluru-based tea and beverage chain Boba Bhai more than doubled its revenue in the fiscal year ending March 2026, but its losses also widened as the Titan Capital-backed company expanded its operations and opened several dozen new stores.
The company’s revenue from operations spiked 139% to Rs 68 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.44 crore in the previous fiscal (FY25), according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


Food and beverage sales, the primary source of revenue, surged 137.1% to Rs 67.26 crore in FY26, accounting for 99% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from scrap sales also increased to Rs 28 lakh from Rs 7 lakh in the previous fiscal year. 

Additionally, the company reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 69 crore in FY26 from Rs 29.44 crore in FY25.

When it comes to costs, Boba Bhai’s cost of materials consumed, the largest expense head, surged 138.5% to Rs 25 crore in FY26, while employee benefit expenses increased 210.3% to Rs 13.5 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses also jumped 139.9% to Rs 13 crore, whereas commission expenses surged 155.9% to Rs 11.44 crore.
Other expenses, which accounted for 35% of the total expenditure, increased 120.3% to Rs 31.46 crore in FY26 Overall, Boba Bhai’s total expenses jumped 2.3X to Rs 90.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 39 crore in the previous fiscal year. Importantly, the company reported 188 employees at the end of  March 2026.
Despite the strong growth in operating revenue, Boba Bhai’s losses widened 2.2X to Rs 21.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 9.96 crore in FY25. However, its operating efficiency improved marginally, with expenses incurred to generate every rupee of operating revenue declining to Rs 1.33 from Rs 1.37 in the previous fiscal year.


Its EBITDA margin improved to -30.35% from -34.67%, while ROCE deteriorated to -41.12% from -32.47%. Meanwhile, cash and bank balances declined sharply to Rs 2.85 crore from Rs 24.07 crore.

Boba Bhai raised Rs 40 crore in March 2026 as it continued to expand its store network. The company currently operates around 100 stores across eight cities and plans to expand to 10 cities in FY27, while adding another 150-200 stores by the end of the fiscal.
The company’s next phase will test whether its expansion can translate into better unit economics. With employee, marketing and material costs rising alongside revenue, Boba Bhai will need to improve store-level profitability and cash generation as it scales.

title: Yulu reports Rs 281 Cr revenue and Rs 97 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
Electric mobility startup Yulu Bikes narrowed its losses by 23% to Rs 96.6 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026. The improvement came as revenue from its electric vehicle rental business increased, while overall expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue.
Yulu’s revenue from operations rose 18.6% to Rs 281 crore in FY26 from Rs 237 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements. 


Income from renting electric vehicles, its largest revenue stream, increased 30.3% to Rs 262 crore from Rs 201 crore and accounted for more than 93% of operating revenue during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
Revenue from the sale of goods declined 59.3% to Rs 9.2 crore while manpower services fell 57% to Rs 5.7 crore from Rs 13.2 crore. In contrast, delivery services revenue rose more than 22X to Rs 2.6 crore. Franchisee income increased 122.2% to Rs 80 lakh from Rs 36 lakh.
Yulu’s employee benefit expenses, its largest cost head, increased 6.8% to Rs 94 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25. Battery-as-a-service costs rose 3.6% to Rs 87 crore, while depreciation expenses declined marginally by 1.5% to Rs 65 crore. Finance costs surged 40.9% to Rs 15.5 crore, whereas the cost of materials consumed fell 60% to Rs 8 crore. Technology and infrastructure expenses increased 11.6% to Rs 15 crore.
Other expenses climbed 34.9% to Rs 92.5 crore from Rs 68.56 crore in FY25. Overall, Yulu’s total expenses increased 7.4% to Rs 377 crore in FY26 from Rs 351 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Bengaluru-based Yulu’s losses narrowed 23% to Rs 97 crore in FY26 from Rs 126 crore in FY25. The company also improved its operating efficiency, with expenses incurred to generate every rupee of operating revenue declining to Rs 1.34 from Rs 1.48 in the previous fiscal year. 


The company’s EBITDA margin improved to -5.89% in FY26 from -15.41% in FY25, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -119.29% compared with -27.26% a year earlier. Meanwhile, Yulu’s cash and bank balance increased to Rs 11.51 crore from Rs 9.65 crore, while total current assets rose to Rs 152 crore from Rs 102 crore.

The financial performance comes as Yulu looks to expand its electric two-wheeler rental network. The company raised $93 million in August 2026 and currently operates a fleet of around 50,000 vehicles. It plans to expand to about 20 cities over the next year and increase its fleet to 200,000 electric vehicles by 2028.
The expansion will require Yulu to scale its fleet and supporting infrastructure, including battery services, while managing the costs associated with operating a larger network.
The deeper push into B2B services is clearly a more attractive and convincing proposition from the firm, which investors have backed despite the poor start with its original consumer rental model in 2017. The losses, expansion plans and rising competition indicate more funding rounds will be needed, which makes the choice of cities and cost control key to success.
Gig workers power the revenue numbers so far, and there remains a strong case to look at other high usage categories to expand the market. While the journey so far has practically seen the market direct Yulu to what actually works, the next stage of the firm's growth puts the onus squarely on the founders to get it right.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 26- Oct 31]
summary:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $115 million across 4 growth-stage deals, 24 early-stage deals including one undisclosed round. The week also saw 6 key appointments and a departure. 

In contrast, 15 startups had collectively secured about $133.9 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $42.34 million across four deals this week, led by Simplismart and Live2.ai, which secured $14 million each. E-commerce brand Troovy raised $11.5 million in a Series B round led by Sharrp Ventures with participation from Info Edge, WaterBridge and Better Capital.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $72.25 million across 24 deals this week, led by healthtech startup Cent, which secured $15 million in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commos. Gaming startup Matiks raised $10 million in its pre-Series A round led by General Catalyst.
E-commerce platform Ace Blend raised $9.91 million in Series A round from 3one4 Capital. Luxury watch brand Rotoris raised Rs 70 crore (about $7.4 million) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures.
Other startups that raised funding this week included fintech brand Mochatrade, gaming startup Let’s Game Now, manufacturing firm Venttup, healthtech startup Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre, QwikBuild and others. 
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding activity with 14 deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR with five deals and Mumbai with three deals. Chennai, Pune, Rourkela, Kerala and Hyderabad also recorded funding this week.

E-commerce startups led the sectors with 8 deals, followed by AI startups which grabbed 6 deals. Meanwhile healthtech, gaming, deeptech, fintech and spiritual tech startups also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 8 deals, followed by pre-seed startups which grabbed 7 deals. Series A, pre-Series A, and pre-Series B also recorded  deals this week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding declined 14% to $115 million from $133.9 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $210 million across 23 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Info Edge founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani will take over as MD and Group CEO of the company from December 3, 2026, as Hitesh Oberoi steps down. Shoonya, the trading and investment platform of Finvasia Group, has appointed Basant Dhawan as its Chief Marketing Officer (CMO). CheQ appointed Rupal Rajal as head of human resources.
Meanwhile, former Criteo executive Medhavi Singh joined Aleph as country head of India and Bellatrix Aerospace appointed Kiran U as CFO.
[Financial results this week]

[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ Air India and SBI card to launch co-branded credit card soon
Air India, India’s leading global airline, and SBI Card, the country’s largest pure-play credit card issuer, have announced a partnership to develop a new Visa-powered co-branded credit card programme. The card will offer a range of travel and lifestyle benefits to members of Air India’s Maharaja Club loyalty programme.
▪️ Pronto founder Anjali Sardana sets up physical AI venture Provision Labs in US
Anjali Sardana, founder of instant household services startup Pronto, has launched Provision Labs, a US-based physical AI venture focused on collecting real-world data to train and test AI systems for robotics and other applications. According to its website, the venture is backed by Lachy Groom, Glade Brook, General Catalyst and Bain Capital Ventures, all of whom have also invested in Pronto. The development comes as Pronto expands its wearable camera rollout through Pronto Verified, an opt-in service that records service sessions and uses anonymised footage for AI training.
▪️ Fibe partners with Hygge to expand rooftop solar financing in India
Digital lending platform Fibe has partnered with Canadian cleantech fintech Hygge Energy to integrate loan financing with digital rooftop solar infrastructure. The collaboration aims to simplify access to solar loans and support the adoption of rooftop solar under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. Hygge Energy, which operates a peer-to-peer rooftop solar trading marketplace in Bengaluru, will extend its platform to connect customers with solar providers and financing options across India.
▪️ Bengaluru-based Pixxel sets up US subsidiary Pixxel Federal to serve defence, intelligence agencies
Spacetech company Pixxel has set up a US subsidiary, Pixxel Federal, to expand its business with American government agencies, including those in defence and intelligence. The unit will offer Earth observation technology, software and satellite systems to federal customers. Pixxel’s hyperspectral imaging technology can identify materials based on how they reflect light, with applications across defence, mineral exploration, environmental monitoring and agriculture. The company already has contracts with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO).
[News flash this week]
▪️ Jio Platforms lists at 21% premium, values company at Rs 12.5 lakh crore
Reliance Industries-backed Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, with shares listing at Rs 1,358 on the NSE, a 21% premium over the issue price of Rs 1,119. The listing valued the company at around Rs 12.5 lakh crore, making it India’s second-largest listed company by market capitalisation. Its Rs 30,213 crore IPO was subscribed 22.19 times, led by QIBs at 70.55 times, while the non-institutional and retail portions saw 14 times and 2.72 times subscription, respectively.
▪️ Skydo secures final GIFT City PSP licence to expand cross-border payments business
Cross-border payments platform Skydo has received final IFSCA authorisation to operate as a Payment Service Provider (PSP) at GIFT City, following in-principle approval in May 2026. The licence will allow it to expand into multi-currency accounts, merchant collections and payment infrastructure for exporters, overseas investment platforms and trade finance providers.
▪️ Ola Electric shares rally nearly 20% ahead of Q2 FY27 results
Ola Electric shares surged 19.5% to Rs 35.78 on October 27, as its Rs 1,000 crore rights issue remained in focus. The issue closes on October 30, with Motilal Oswal and Calliope Capital applying for 2.39 crore shares. Meanwhile, SoftBank affiliate SVF II Ostrich reduced its stake from 12.9% to 11.7% through share and rights entitlement sales, according to a regulatory filing.
▪️ Entrackr takes The Spur D2C Community mixer to Bengaluru
Entrackr’s D2C community initiative, The Spur, held its second edition in Bengaluru on October 23, bringing together over 30 founders and business leaders for informal discussions on building and scaling consumer brands. Hosted at The Bier Library and supported by PhonePe Payment Gateway, the event skipped panels and pitches in favour of candid conversations about business challenges and lessons from experience. The Bengaluru edition followed the inaugural gathering in Gurugram on September 25, which brought together over 40 founders and 10 investors from the NCR D2C ecosystem.
▪️ Virat Kohli raises stake in Agilitas Sports to 6.4% following one8 merger
Cricketer Virat Kohli has increased his stake in Agilitas Sports to 6.4% from 1.8% following the merger of his sportswear brand one8 with the company, Agilitas said in a statement on October 29. Kohli had earlier invested Rs 40 crore in Agilitas at a valuation of Rs 3,100 crore and made no fresh investment to increase his stake. The merger of One8 Sports Pvt Ltd with Agilitas Sports Pvt Ltd was approved by the Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

title: Delhivery reports Rs 3,066 Cr revenue and Rs 41 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
summary:
Logistics company Delhivery reported a 19.8% year-on-year growth in revenue in the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q2 FY27) and remained profitable during the period.
Delhivery’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 3,066 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,559 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


The company primarily generates revenue from its logistics services, including freight handling, transportation and warehousing. It also recorded other income of Rs 67 crore, taking its total income to Rs 3,133 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,652 crore in Q2 FY26.
Freight, handling and servicing costs remained Delhivery’s largest expense, accounting for 70.97% of its total expenses. This cost increased 19.1% to Rs 2,195 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,843 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Employee benefit expenses increased 4.7% to Rs 446 crore from Rs 426 crore, while depreciation rose 11% to Rs 197.5 crore from Rs 178 crore. Finance costs declined 12.8% to Rs 34 crore, whereas other expenses remained largely flat at Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27.
Overall, the company’s total expenses rose 14.2% to Rs 3,093 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,708 crore in Q2 FY26.
Delhivery posted a net profit of Rs 40.64 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 50.50 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had also posted a profit of Rs 32 crore in the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q1 FY27).
On a half-yearly basis, Delhivery’s operating revenue grew 23.6% to Rs 5,997 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 4,853 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 78.9% to Rs 72.55 crore from Rs 40.55 crore during the same period.
Delhivery’s shares closed at Rs 386 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 29,831 crore.

title: PB Fintech Q2 FY27 profit rises 43% to Rs 192 Cr, revenue up 35%
summary:
PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, reported a strong financial performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue registering a healthy year-on-year growth alongside a 43% increase in net profit compared to the corresponding quarter last year.

The company’s revenue from operations grew 35% to Rs 2,178 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,614 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the stock exchanges.


In terms of revenue composition, insurance broker services contributed Rs 2,015.19 crore to the company’s revenue, up 41.1% year on year from Rs 1,428.16 crore. Revenue from other services declined 12.3% to Rs 162.52 crore from Rs 185.39 crore.
On the expense front, Employee benefits, the company’s largest expense, increased 28.8% to Rs 773 crore. Advertising expenses surged 59.5% to Rs 447 crore, while network and internet costs jumped 65.1% to Rs 70.75 crore. Depreciation and amortisation stood at Rs 43.78 crore.

Other expenses rose 21.8% to Rs 733 crore. Consequently, the company’s total expenses increased 32.6% to Rs 2,067.66 crore in Q2 FY27.
The Gurugram-based company’s net profit stood at Rs 193 crore, compared to Rs 135 crore in Q2 FY26. 

For the first half of FY27, the company’s revenue from operations increased 37.3% to Rs 4,066 crore, compared with Rs 2,962 crore in the corresponding period last year. Its profit after tax surged 61.4% to Rs 355 crore from Rs 220 crore in the same period.

Since the end of Q1 FY27, PB Fintech’s share price has declined 38.3% to Rs 1,000 from Rs 1,620. Its market capitalisation also fell 37.2% to Rs 47,104 crore from Rs 74,957 crore during the same period.

title: Atomberg gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
summary:
Consumer appliances maker Atomberg Technologies has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 7.65 crore shares by existing shareholders. The company is yet to announce the price band and timeline for the issue.
Atomberg plans to use Rs 90 crore from the fresh issue proceeds to repay or prepay its borrowings. It will allocate Rs 150 crore towards brand awareness and performance marketing activities, while another Rs 100 crore will be used for research and development (R&D). The remaining amount will go towards general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2012 by Manoj Meena, who was joined by Sibabrata Das as co-founder in 2013, Atomberg initially focused on energy-efficient ceiling fans. It has since expanded its portfolio to include mixer grinders, water purifiers, cold-pressed juicers and other consumer appliances.
Apart from its consumer appliance business, the company also manufactures and supplies proprietary motors, controllers and other components to enterprise customers such as Voltas, Godrej and Blue Star through its subsidiary, Atomberg Innovations.
On the financial front, Atomberg's revenue from operations increased 34.8% to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its adjusted EBITDA declined to Rs 37.12 crore during the fiscal year from Rs 51.35 crore in FY25. The company reported a loss of Rs 148.88 crore in FY26, narrowing from Rs 199.08 crore in FY24.
Atomberg has also seen partial exits by existing investors ahead of its proposed listing. A91 Partners, which has backed the company since 2019, has sold shares worth around Rs 445 crore while retaining a 21% stake, according to the company's IPO disclosures.
ICICI Securities, Avendus Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

title: Traya nears Rs 600 Cr revenue in FY26, posts Rs 29 Cr loss
summary:
What began as an attempt to address hair loss and the insecurities surrounding it among India’s youth has turned Traya into a nearly Rs 600 crore business. Yet, despite strong revenue growth in FY26, the seven-year-old haircare startup continued to report losses.
Traya's revenue from operations surged 72.6% year-on-year to Rs 585 crore in FY26 from Rs 339 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

Founded in 2019, Traya focuses on addressing hair loss by identifying its root causes and provides personalised hair treatment plans supported by consultations with hair coaches and licensed physicians.
The sale of customised hair care kits was Traya's sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 8 crore through gains from the sale of investments, pushing its total income to Rs 593 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 343 crore in FY25.
On the cost side, advertising remained the largest expense, accounting for around 44% of the firm's total expenditure. Advertising costs nearly doubled to Rs 275 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, the cost of materials procured increased 68.7% to Rs 140 crore during the last fiscal year.
Traya spent Rs 81 crore on employee benefits in FY26. Its legal, transportation, technology and other overheads also catalyzed its total expenditure up 70.2% to Rs 623 crore in FY26 from Rs 366 crore in FY25.
Despite a 72.6% growth in operating revenue, the increase in expenses continued to weigh on the company's bottom line. Traya reported a net loss of Rs 29 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.5 crore in FY25.
At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.06 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -44.7% and -6.19%, respectively. The company had total current assets of Rs 174 crore as of March 2026.
Traya has raised approximately Rs 96 crore in funding to date. This includes a Rs 75 crore investment from Xponentia Capital in April 2024. Its backers include Fireside Ventures, Kae Capital and Whiteboard Capital. The firm is reportedly in talks to raise another Rs 300 crore from Verlinvest.
Hair thinning and hair loss are real concerns, particularly among India's youth. Factors such as water quality, nutritional deficiencies, eating habits, and poor sleep can all contribute to the problem. This has created an opportunity for startups to build businesses around hair care, with several brands now selling gummies, serums and supplements. Traya has managed to carve out a place in this growing market with its personalised treatment approach. It will be interesting to see how large this business can become and how soon the company can turn profitable.

title: Smartworks posts Rs 591 Cr revenue and Rs 26 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
summary:
Managed office space provider Smartworks reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27). The company posted a 39% year-on-year growth in revenue during the period. Meanwhile, its EBITDA grew 37% to Rs 391 crore.
Smartworks’ revenue from operations rose to Rs 591 crore in the Q2 FY27 from Rs 425 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Smartworks derives the bulk of its operating revenue from the development, design and licensing of serviced office spaces, along with fit-out services and other ancillary offerings. The company also reported Rs 14 crore in non-operating income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 605 crore in Q2 FY27.
On a sequential basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 8% from Rs 546 crore in Q1 FY27.
On the cost side, depreciation related to lease expenses was the largest expense for Smartworks at Rs 259 crore, up 31% from Rs 198 crore in Q2 FY26. This was followed by operating expenses, which stood at Rs 172 crore during the quarter. Employee benefits expenses amounted to Rs 28 crore. Finance costs and other overheads took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 570 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 445 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
At the bottom line, Smartworks continued its profitability on a quarter-on-quarter basis and turned profitable on a year-on-year basis, reporting a net profit of Rs 26 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to a net loss of Rs 3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Meanwhile its EBITDA grew 37% year-on-year to Rs 391 crore during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of over 66%.
For H1 FY27, Smartworks’ operating revenue grew 42% year-on-year to Rs 1,138 crore. The company also reported a net profit of Rs 39 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 7.3 crore in H1 FY26. 
As of 11:22 AM today, Smartworks shares traded at around Rs 477.7 apiece, valuing the company at a market capitalization of Rs 5,465 crore ($575 million).

title: Starbucks India brews Rs 1,367 Cr revenue in FY26; cuts losses by 27%
summary:
Tata Starbucks, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata Consumer Products and Starbucks Corporation, has established itself as one of India’s largest coffee chains by revenue and store count. While the company has grown over the years, its bottom line remains in the red.
Starbucks’ revenue from operations grew a modest 7% year-on-year to Rs 1,367 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,277 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Incorporated in September 2011, the company operates cafes across India under the Starbucks brand. By 2025, Tata Starbucks had expanded to over 390 stores across 54 Indian cities, with approximately 4,300 partners (employees). Importantly, the company aims to expand its network to around 1,000 stores by 2028.
The sale of coffee and related products accounted for most of its revenue. The remaining income came from its loyalty programme, My Starbucks Rewards, through which customers earn loyalty points called Stars.
The procurement of coffee beans and other related products accounted for 24% of the company’s total expenditure. This cost increased 6% to Rs 356 crore in FY26 from Rs 336 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose 9.8% to Rs 225 crore during the same period.
Rent, electricity, advertising, freight and other overheads took total expenses up 4.7% to Rs 1,514 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,446 crore in FY25.
With controlled spending, Starbucks narrowed its net loss by 27% to Rs 99 crore in FY26 from Rs 136 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA stood at Rs 234 crore during the year.
At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.11 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. On a standalone basis, its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -2.6%, while its EBITDA margin was 17%.
Its closest competitor, Café Coffee Day, reported revenue of Rs 1,094 crore and a net profit of Rs 14 crore. Starbucks also competes with several newer coffee brands, including Blue Tokai, Rage Coffee, Third Wave Coffee Roasters, Slay Coffee, Sleepy Owl and Seven Beans Co.
As newer coffee brands build their own loyal customer base, competition in India’s coffee market is getting stronger. For Starbucks, the challenge is not just to expand its store network but to get customers to keep coming back for its premium offerings. The question is whether India’s appetite for expensive coffee is deep enough to support its ambitious expansion plans while bringing its bottom line into the black. For Starbucks, a business that looks unlikely to hit the $200 million mark by 2030  raises its own issues of attention and perhaps, even relevance, if profits remain elusive.

title: Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre raises Rs 28 Cr in Series A round led by Alkemi
summary:
Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre, a provider of mental health, addiction and dementia care services, has raised Rs 28 crore in a Series A funding round led by Alkemi Growth Capital.
The fresh funds will be used to enter new geographies, expand clinical and staff capacity, develop specialised care programmes, and deepen insurance and corporate partnerships, Jagruti said in a press release.
The funding comes amid growing demand for structured mental health and rehabilitation services in India. However, the sector remains fragmented, with care largely delivered through standalone clinics and smaller independent establishments.
Founded by Amar Shinde, Vijaya Shinde and Hemant Shinde, Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre provides residential care for mental health conditions, addiction and dementia. The Pune-based organisation operates more than 19 centres across nine cities, with over 1,600 beds and a team of more than 40 doctors.
Jagruti plans to expand to over 40 centres and more than 4,000 beds across Tier I and Tier II cities over the next three to four years. The organisation claims to have treated more than 82,000 individuals.
Its centres are spread across cities including Pune, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Chennai. The organisation offers programmes for mental health conditions, addiction and substance use disorders, and neurological care.
The investment expands Alkemi Growth Capital's exposure to healthcare delivery and adjacent segments. Its portfolio includes Redcliffe Labs in diagnostics, Medvital in medical devices, Datar Cancer Genetics in in-vitro diagnostics (IVD), Medulance in emergency medical response, Alphadroid in autonomous mobility robots, and Leumas in physical AI for pharmaceutical manufacturing.
Jagruti is Alkemi's first investment in the mental health and rehabilitation segment of healthcare delivery.

title: Docterz raises Rs 5 Cr from Vineeta Singh, Avnish Anand and 20 doctor-investors
summary:
Docterz, a healthcare technology startup founded by paediatrician Dr Atish Laddad, has raised Rs 5 crore from around 35 investors, including doctors who use its platform.
Around 20 doctor users contributed nearly Rs 3 crore, accounting for about 60% of the total funding. The investor group also includes Vineeta Singh, co-founder and CEO of SUGAR Cosmetics, and Avnish Anand, co-founder and former CEO of CaratLane.
The company plans to use the funds to expand organically, explore acquisitions and develop AI tools for doctors. It also aims to expand its reach among independent practitioners, smaller clinics and healthcare organisations across India.
Founded over a decade ago, Docterz offers an integrated platform for electronic medical records, appointments, billing, vaccination management and patient engagement. Its technology supports more than 5,000 doctors across India, with a strong presence in paediatrics.
The company is also developing AI-enabled tools to help doctors with documentation, administrative workflows, practice data analysis and patient follow-ups.
Dr Dhananjay Sangle, a paediatrician and Docterz investor, said his decision to invest was based on his experience using the platform for several years and his confidence in its founder.
Vineeta Singh said customer participation in a funding round was a strong signal for a business, adding that doctors investing in Docterz reflected their trust in the platform and its founder.
Dr Suhas Warad, another paediatrician and investor in the company, said technology designed around doctors’ needs could help them manage their practices more efficiently and devote more time to patient care.

title: Physical AI startup Tensrai raises Rs 3.4 Cr in pre-seed round
summary:
Hyderabad-based Physical AI startup Tensrai has raised Rs 3.4 crore in a pre-seed funding  from India Accelerator, Finvolve, Hyderabad Angels and other angels.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate technology development, strengthen engineering and deployment capabilities, and support expansion into domestic and international markets, Tensrai said in a press release.
Co-founded by Sai Nikhil Rao Gona, Venkata Sai Charan Chalamalasetty, Harshith Uppalapati, and Vivek Datta, Tensrai is developing a unified, retrofittable autonomy platform that enables industrial and commercial robots, vehicles and machines to perform physical tasks autonomously.
The platform combines vision-first navigation, AI-based localisation, vision-language model (VLM)-powered reasoning, autonomous mobility, robotic arm manipulation and vision-language-action (VLA)-based teach-and-deploy capabilities. The technology is designed to help machines perceive their surroundings, reason through tasks, learn skills and execute operations with limited human intervention.
Tensrai aims to bring autonomous capabilities to both purpose-built machines and existing equipment through retrofitting, potentially reducing the cost and complexity of adopting robotics across industrial and commercial settings.
The startup is targeting applications such as autonomous material handling and cleaning across factories, warehouses, airports, hospitals, shopping malls and commercial campuses. It is also developing a general-purpose mobile manipulator that combines autonomous mobility with robotic arms to perform tasks across material handling, cleaning, manufacturing and construction.
Tensrai plans to generate revenue through multiple streams, including robot sales, autonomy retrofitting, Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) and customised solutions. It also plans to expand into international markets.
The funding comes amid growing interest in Physical AI, which combines artificial intelligence with robotic systems and machines to enable them to understand and interact with the physical world. Unlike software-based AI applications, Physical AI systems are designed to translate perception and reasoning into real-world actions.
With a common autonomy platform for different types of machines, Tensrai aims to help businesses automate repetitive, labour-intensive and operationally complex tasks across industrial and commercial settings.

title: BlackBuck’s Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 56% to Rs 235 Cr, profit grows 42%

title: CureSkin posts Rs 133 Cr revenue and Rs 35 Cr loss in FY26
summary:
Skincare and dermatology startup CureSkin improved its financial performance in FY26, with higher revenue from product sales and services and lower advertising and promotional costs helping reduce its losses. 
The firm’s revenue from operations grew 27.9% to Rs 133 crore in FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies.


The Bengaluru-based company offers personalised skincare and haircare solutions through digital consultations and products recommended for individual skin and hair concerns. Its business combines product sales with services, including dermatology-led consultations.
Product sales remained its primary revenue source, accounting for about 91% of operating revenue. Revenue from products increased 17.1% to Rs 120.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 103 crore in FY25. Revenue from services, meanwhile, rose nearly ninefold to Rs 12.4 crore, albeit on a smaller base. The increase points to a larger contribution from services, although product sales continued to account for most of the business.
The firm also reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking total revenue to Rs 134 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 108 crore a year earlier.
CureSkin’s advertising and promotional spend fell by 17.6% to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 74 crore a year earlier, reducing one of its major cost heads. The decline helped bring down overall expenditure despite higher spending on materials and other operating costs.
The cost of materials consumed increased 15.4% to Rs 42 crore, broadly tracking the rise in product sales. Employee benefit expenses, however, declined 5.3% to Rs 23.6 crore from Rs 24.9 crore, adding to the savings from lower promotional spending.
Among the remaining cost heads, transportation expenses increased 30% to Rs 13 crore, while legal and professional charges fell 36.5% to Rs 7.2 crore. Miscellaneous expenses rose 14.8% to Rs 22.2 crore from Rs 19 crore.
CureSkin’s net loss narrowed 48.5% to Rs 35 crore in FY26 from Rs 68 crore in FY25, supported by higher revenue and lower overall expenditure.


Its EBITDA margin improved to -21.81% from -60.94% in the previous fiscal year. On a unit basis, CureSkin spent Rs 1.27 to earn every rupee of operating revenue, compared with Rs 1.69 in FY25, indicating lower costs relative to revenue, though the company remained loss-making.
As of March 2026, CureSkin had cash and bank balances of Rs 8 crore and current assets of Rs 40 crore, down from Rs 72 crore a year earlier. The firm has raised $26 million to date, including a $20 million led by HealthQuad. Its other investors include JSW, Khosla Ventures and Sharrp Ventures.
CureSkin’s next phase will depend on its ability to sustain demand for its products while expanding its services business. The sharp decline in losses suggests that tighter cost management has improved its financial performance, but the company will need to maintain this discipline as it scales. Growing its services revenue could also help diversify its income beyond product sales. With marketing remaining a significant expense, balancing customer acquisition with repeat purchases and revenue growth will be important for building a more sustainable business model.

title: Venttup raises $3 Mn in pre Series A round led by Rainmatter, Unicorn India Ventures

The fresh capital will be used to expand the engineering team, invest in precision manufacturing facilities and rapid prototyping infrastructure, and adopt AI to improve B2B sourcing, supplier intelligence and operational efficiency, the company said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Sandeep Nair, M. Wasim Ankli and Joseph Panakkal, Venttup is a B2B manufacturing company focused on the localisation and development of critical and precision components and subassemblies.
Through its Manufacturing as a Service (MaaS) model, the company supports customers across engineering design, specification standardisation, rapid prototyping, testing, validation and contract manufacturing.
According to the Bengaluru-based startup, its capabilities include precision machining, casting and forging, sheet metal fabrication, box builds, special purpose machines, industrial automation, robotics and technology-enabled B2B sourcing. It combines in-house engineering capabilities with a network of MSME manufacturing partners to serve sectors such as energy, data centres, mobility, defence, aerospace and space.
Venttup is also setting up a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru to strengthen its rapid prototyping and precision manufacturing capabilities. The facility will support precision machining, turning and sheet metal production for applications in energy transition, defence, aerospace and space. It is expected to help shorten the time from component development and validation to production readiness and mass manufacturing.
The company said it grew fivefold to Rs 10 crore in FY26. Over the past 12 months, it has added more than 15 large companies to its customer base and built a business opportunity pipeline of around Rs 30 crore across new energy, mobility and smart infrastructure.
Venttup plans to expand across four business verticals: energy transition and data centres; aerospace, defence and space systems; smart infrastructure and future mobility; and electronics, automation and smart manufacturing.

title: Servify cuts losses to Rs 51 Cr in FY26; US contributes 60% of business
summary:
Post-sales service firm Servify reported a marginal 4% decline in revenue in FY26 (year ended March 2026), dragged by consecutive degrowth in its India business. However, the company made meaningful progress on the bottom line and narrowed losses by 40% to Rs 51 crore during the period.
Following a 16% increase in FY25, Servify’s revenue from operations declined to Rs 751 crore in FY26 from Rs 781 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its annual consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2015, Servify provides brand-authorised after-sales support for mobile phones, gadgets, electronics, and home appliances. The company has partnerships with major brands, including Apple, Bose, and HP, and operates across 18,000 service locations in more than 40 countries. It also processes over 2.8 lakh claims annually, according to its website.
White-labelled protection plans sold through mobile apps and web portals remain Servify’s primary revenue engine, which  contributed over 97% of total operating income. The segment declined 4% to Rs 730 crore in FY26. Income from mobile handset and spare parts sales also fell 13% to Rs 20 crore during the period.
For the second consecutive year, the US remained Servify’s largest market, which contributed nearly 60% of its total revenue at Rs 448 crore in FY26, a 12% year-on-year increase. In contrast, revenue from India declined 27% to Rs 242 crore from Rs 330 crore in FY25. The remaining revenue came from other markets, including Europe, Canada, the United Arab Emirates, and Turkey.
For the post sales firm, insurance premiums and repair expenses formed the bulk of Servify’s direct operating costs at Rs 439 crore in FY26, followed by commission expenses of Rs 82 crore. The remaining costs included courier charges, service and upcountry charges, and mobile handset consumption, which together totalled Rs 23 crore. Overall, direct operating costs declined 7% to Rs 555 crore during the fiscal year and accounted for 69% of total expenses.
The firm’s employee benefit expenses dropped 10.6% to Rs 135 crore in FY26 from Rs 151 crore in the previous fiscal year. These expenses included Rs 14 crore in employee stock option (ESOP) costs.
Information technology, legal and professional fees, depreciation and amortisation, along with other overheads, took Servify’s total expenses to Rs 807 crore in FY26, an 8% decrease from Rs 876 crore in FY25, in line with the decline in revenue.
The moderation in operating scale was accompanied by lower expenses, which helped Servify narrow its losses by 40% to Rs 51 crore in FY26 from Rs 85 crore in FY25.

Servify’s ROCE and EBITDA margin remained negative at 16.67% and 2.47%, respectively, while its EBITDA loss stood at Rs 19 crore in FY26. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.07 to generate every rupee of operating revenue during the fiscal year.
At the end of March 2025, Servify reported total current assets of Rs 590 crore, along with a cash and bank balance of Rs 64 crore.
Backed by Blume Ventures, Servify has raised over $135 million to date, including a $65 million Series D led by Singularity Growth Opportunities Fund. In March 2025, it raised an additional $7.8 million in its ongoing Series D from BEENEXT, valuing the company at around $700 million.
Servify operates in a competitive device protection and after-sales services market, where players such as Assurant and SquareTrade offer protection plans and repair services. While the US business cushioned the decline in India, the 27% drop in domestic revenue highlighted the challenge of sustaining growth across markets. Lower expenses helped narrow losses, but Servify’s negative EBITDA margin and spending of Rs 1.07 for every rupee of operating revenue showed that the company still needed to improve operating efficiency to reach profitability.

Founded in 2023 by Shirley Setia, Jinsoon Lee, Mayank Jain and Sakshi Jain, ISLAND Beauty focuses on barrier-focused skincare products designed for regular use.
The brand sources ingredients from South Korea and develops its formulations in India, with a focus on local weather conditions and consumers’ skincare needs.

title: Bijnis rebrands as Zorit, raises Rs 27 Cr led by Sparrow Capital
summary:
B2B quick commerce startup Zorit, formerly known as Bijnis, has raised nearly Rs 27 crore ($2.84 million) in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital. Existing investors Info Edge and WaterBridge participated in the round, along with Better Capital, angel investors and employees.
The angel investors include Anupam Mittal, founder of Shaadi.com, the founders of Shiprocket, Mohit Sardana, CEO of Xpressbees, and Sarthak Misra of SoftBank.
Following the investment, Info Edge’s shareholding in Bijnis will increase to 20.12% on a fully converted and diluted basis. In a stock exchange disclosure earlier this week, Info Edge said it may also acquire additional equity in the company through a secondary transaction.
Founded in 2015 by Siddharth Vij, Chaitanya Rathi, Siddharth Rastogi and Sachin Chauhan, Zorit initially operated as a B2B marketplace connecting manufacturers with retailers. The company transitioned to an inventory led quick commerce model in late 2024.
Zorit enables offline retailers to source inventory from locally stocked dark stores, with deliveries in as little as 60 minutes. The platform operates 12 dark stores across 12 cities and has reached Rs 120 crore in annualised sales. Nearly 50% of its dark stores have achieved break even, including the cost of liquidating unsold inventory.
According to the company, nearly 60% of its retailers had never used an online B2B platform before. Retailer retention beyond the sixth month has improved fourfold compared with its previous model, while monthly ordering frequency has increased fivefold. Retailers place an average of five to six orders per month, with top cohorts exceeding 10 orders.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its quick commerce infrastructure, expand its product assortment and deepen retailer engagement across its operating markets.
“We strongly believe that a substantial part of India’s future commerce will remain retailer led. As consumer expectations evolve, retailers need better technology and supply chain infrastructure to compete and grow,” said Siddharth Vij, CEO of Zorit.
In May 2023, Info Edge wrote off its entire investment of Rs 76.65 crore in Bijnis, operated by Bizcrum Infotech Pvt Ltd.
The startup had previously raised capital from investors including Matrix Partners (now Z47), Sequoia Capital (now Peak XV Partners) and WestBridge Capital. Bijnis raised $30 million in a Series B round led by WestBridge Capital in September 2021 and had secured over $40 million in total funding.
With its shift to quick commerce, Zorit is focusing on faster inventory replenishment, locally relevant product assortments and lower minimum order values for offline retailers.

title: Astrotalk’s profit jumps 10X to Rs 222 Cr in FY26; overseas biz grows 2.6X
summary:
Astrology and spiritual wellness platform Astrotalk’s net profit surged more than 10-fold to Rs 222 crore in FY26, as revenue grew 55% year-on-year to cross Rs 1,800 crore. International markets drove a significant share of this growth, with overseas revenue growing 2.6 times. 
The expansion came alongside a sharp increase in advertising and expenses, which more than doubled to Rs 823 crore as the Noida-based company invested in its growth.
The firm’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,823 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,176 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements.

Astrotalk operates a digital astrology platform that connects users with astrologers for paid consultations via chat, calls and video. Revenue from consultations rose 45% to Rs 1,657 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,139 crore in FY25, and accounted for around 91% of operating revenue. 
International revenue surged 2.6 times to Rs 621 crore from Rs 236 crore, with its share of total revenue at 34% against 20% a year earlier. Revenue from India rose 28% to Rs 1,202 crore, while international markets added Rs 385 crore of new revenue during the year, more than half of Astrotalk’s total revenue growth.
Beyond consultations, Astrotalk has expanded into e-commerce through Astrotalk Store, which sells certified Rudraksha, gemstones, crystals and Vastu products via its own platform and marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart and Blinkit. Revenue from the segment jumped 4.4 times to Rs 166 crore in FY26 from Rs 37 crore in FY25.
Commenting on the expansion, Puneet Gupta, founder and CEO of Astrotalk, said, “We set out to build a diversified, global business from India, and FY26 shows it is working. A third of our revenue now comes from outside India, and Astrotalk Store has grown into a real second business.”
Looking at the expenses, advertising and business promotion expenses more than doubled to Rs 823 crore from Rs 337 crore, accounting for 52.2% of total expenses, as Astrotalk ramped up marketing to support its growth. Legal and professional expenses rose 6.8% to Rs 550 crore from Rs 515 crore, which includes payments to astrologers for consultations
Employee benefit expenses, meanwhile, declined 56% to Rs 63 crore from Rs 143 crore in FY25, because of sharp reductions in ESOP related costs to Rs 9 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 72 crore in FY25.
Other expenses, including software and website costs, payment gateway charges and shipping expenses, contributed to Astrotalk’s total expenditure of Rs 1,576 crore in FY26, a 38% year-on-year increase from Rs 1,140 crore in FY25.
Astrotalk’s net profit surged to Rs 222 crore in FY26 from Rs 22 crore in FY25, despite heavy spending on advertising and business promotion. The company’s expansion beyond consultations into e-commerce, along with its growing international business, supported the performance.
Its ROCE and EBITDA margin improved to 30.8% and 13.83%, respectively. On a unit level, the company spent Re 0.86 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in  the last fiscal year.

As of March 2026, Astrotalk had total current assets of Rs 653 crore, including Rs 141 crore in cash and bank balances.
Astrotalk’s FY26 performance showed strong revenue growth and a sharp improvement in profitability, supported by overseas expansion and the growth of its e-commerce business. However, the gains came alongside higher advertising expenditure, which more than doubled to Rs 823 crore and accounted for over half of total expenses. While international markets and Astrotalk Store added new revenue streams, paid consultations remained the core business. The company’s ability to sustain growth while managing customer acquisition costs and diversifying revenue will remain key to its financial performance.

summary:
E-commerce marketplace Meesho has announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 34% year on year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 68% to Rs 132 crore during the same period.
The company’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 4,132 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 3,074 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements filed with the NSE.

Meesho did not disclose its revenue breakdown in the quarterly financial statements. The company reported Rs 127 crore in non-operating income, which took its total income to Rs 4,259 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue from operations rose 11% from Rs 3,713 crore in Q1 FY27.
Meesho did not disclose most of its expenses in the quarterly financial statements. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 281 crore in Q2 FY27, an 18% increase from Rs 237 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Its depreciation expense stood at Rs 20 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenses grew 24% year on year to Rs 4,382 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 3,540 crore in Q2 FY26.

title: Exclusive: Dainik Bhaskar family office invests in spiritual tech startup Vama
summary:
Spiritual tech startup Vama has raised Rs 19.03 crore (approximately $2.1 million) in an ongoing Pre-Series A funding round led by Writers and Publishers Private Limited, the family office of Dainik Bhaskar. The round also saw participation from Wavemaker Partners, Silver Needle Ventures, Harit Nagpal, MD and CEO of Tata Play, Swati Parikh, Vinay Mittal and Nikhil Bhandarkar.
According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Vama allotted 3,452 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 55,134.39 per share, aggregating to Rs 19.03 crore.
The round appears to be ongoing, with the Delhi based company likely to raise additional capital in subsequent tranches.
Dainik Bhaskar’s family office led the round with an investment of Rs 12.50 crore, while the remaining Rs 6.53 crore came from the other investors, including Wavemaker Partners, Silver Needle Ventures, Harit Nagpal, Swati Parikh, Vinay Mittal and Nikhil Bhandarkar.
Vama could be among the first recorded startup investments by the Dainik Bhaskar family office.

Founded in 2020 by Acharya Dev and Manu Jain, Vama provides devotees access to temple services, astrology consultations and spiritual products through its platform. Temple services account for around 70% of its revenue, while astrology and Vama Mall contribute the rest.
Dainik Bhaskar’s presence across Hindi speaking markets could help Vama expand its reach and strengthen its access to temples and other service providers.
Following the allotment, Dainik Bhaskar’s family office holds around 6.98% stake in Vama. Co-founders Manu Jain and Acharya Dev, also known as Sandeep Chandra Tiwari, hold 14.44% and 14.43% stakes, respectively.

title: Jio Platforms lists at 21% premium, values company at Rs 12.5 lakh crore
summary:
Reliance Industries-backed Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, with its shares listing at a premium of around 21% over the issue price of Rs 1,119.
The shares listed at Rs 1,358 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), giving investors a gain of Rs 239 per share. At the listing price, the company commanded a market capitalisation of around Rs 12.5 lakh crore, making it India’s second-largest listed company by market value.
The listing follows Jio Platforms’ Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering (IPO), which was subscribed 22.19 times during its three-day bidding period between October 21 and October 23.
Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion 70.55 times. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 14 times, while the retail portion saw 2.72 times subscription.
The IPO comprised a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 1,065-1,119 per share.
Jio Platforms had raised Rs 8,110 crore from 212 anchor investors ahead of the public issue. The anchor book attracted bids worth nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore, more than 30 times the amount allocated to these investors. Participants included global investors such as BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity Investments and T. Rowe Price, along with domestic mutual funds and insurers.
The company plans to use Rs 27,500 crore from the IPO proceeds to repay part of the borrowings of its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
Jio Platforms houses Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital businesses, including Reliance Jio Infocomm, which offers mobile connectivity, fixed broadband and digital services. It has also been expanding its presence in 5G, digital applications and artificial intelligence.
Reliance Jio Infocomm had 533.3 million subscribers at the end of June 2026. Global technology companies Meta and Google also invested in Jio Platforms in 2020, alongside several private equity firms and institutional investors.

title: Skincare brand CHOSEN raises extended Series A round from Wellbeing Nutrition founders
summary:
Skincare brand CHOSEN has raised an extension of its Series A round from Avnish Chhabria and Saurabh Kapoor, founders of Wellbeing Nutrition.
Prior to this, the Chennai based startup had raised $5 million in a Series A round led by Fireside Ventures in May this year. The round also saw participation from BOLD, L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund, Alkemi Growth Capital and other angel investors. CHOSEN had previously raised $1.2 million in an angel funding round in 2024.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its R&D capabilities and expand its formulation pipeline across topical skincare and nutraceuticals, with a focus on clinical validation and dermatological research, CHOSEN said in a press release.
Founded in 2020 by Renita Rajan, CHOSEN develops skincare products for melanin rich Indian skin. Its approach draws on the science of the exposome, which examines how environmental factors affect skin health, and focuses on four areas of ageing: pigmentation, skin texture, facial contour and hair ageing.
The company plans to establish a Centre of Excellence to involve dermatologists in product development and research. It also plans to expand its R&D, brand and growth teams as it enters its next phase of expansion.
CHOSEN’s portfolio spans more than 50 products across skincare, haircare, body care and nutraceuticals. Its products are prescribed by more than 2,000 doctors. In 2026, CHOSEN Sculpt became India's first topical lower face contouring serum, backed by a 12 week clinical study involving Indian women published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology.
The company sells its products through its website and platforms such as Amazon, Myntra, Swiggy, FirstClub and Distacart. It serves most serviceable pin codes in India, with Chennai, Coimbatore, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune, Ahmedabad and Goa among its priority markets.
CHOSEN also ships to international markets, including the US, the UK, Australia, Canada, the UAE, Singapore, France, Sweden, Portugal, the Czech Republic, Hong Kong and Thailand.
The brand competes with skincare companies such as Avène, Heliocare, Cetaphil, Sebamed, Shiseido and Dr. Sturm.

title: Simplismart raises $14 Mn from Dallas Venture Capital, NVIDIA and others
summary:
AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its inference engine and orchestration platform, expand its cloud provider network and support its growth across North America and other global markets.
Entrackr had earlier reported on the deal, which values the company at around $100 million post money. Previously, Simplismart raised $7 million in a Series A round in October 2024.
Founded by Amritanshu Jain, Simplismart provides infrastructure that helps enterprises deploy and run AI models while optimising inference costs, latency and GPU utilisation. Its platform also enables cloud providers to convert their GPU capacity into AI services for enterprise customers.
The company said its annualised revenue run rate grew 14X over the past six months. Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema, which use its platform for production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.
Simplismart also works with cloud providers to offer managed AI inference services. At Yotta, its platform powers the serverless inference layer of Shakti Studio, which allows customers to run AI models without managing the underlying infrastructure.
Unlike inference providers that procure or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart focuses on the software layer that enables third party GPU infrastructure to support production AI workloads. The company is also working with cloud providers and sovereign AI programmes across India, North America, the Middle East, Australia and East Asia.
The startup plans to use the new capital to further develop its inference and orchestration capabilities and build partnerships aimed at matching AI workloads with available GPU capacity across regions and cloud environments.

title: IvyCap Ventures leads Rs 130 Cr pre-Series B round in Live2.ai
summary:
Live2.ai, an AI-based social intelligence and commerce activation platform, has raised Rs 130 crore (about $14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round comprises primary capital for business growth and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.
The fresh funds will be used to develop its agentic intelligence layer, expand its go-to-market operations for enterprise and global consumer brands, and strengthen its regional cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific, Live2.ai said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by J Venkat, Neha Suyal and Yash Arora, Live2.ai provides a platform that connects social intelligence with campaign execution and commerce activation.
The platform helps brands monitor online conversations, plan and publish social media posts, track performance, manage audits and compliance for influencer and user-generated content, and convert rights-cleared content into shoppable experiences across digital and offline channels.
The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform combines a unified entity graph, multimodal AI and autonomous AI agents. It monitors brand conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X and review sites to help brands identify trends and inform business decisions.
Live2.ai offers three key capabilities: social intelligence for trend identification and campaign strategy; audit and compliance management for influencer and user-generated content; and social publishing and performance tracking across channels.
The platform also uses eight AI agents, including Crisis Detection, Trend Scout, Campaign Auditor and Autonomous Response, to support tasks across social intelligence, campaign management and customer engagement. These agents operate on a shared entity graph with governance controls and human review.
Live2.ai said it works with brands such as Henkel's Schwarzkopf, Salonory, Titan Brands and Shiseido. The company claims to serve more than 200 brands across the US, Europe and Southeast Asia.
The startup said its revenue grew fourfold in the past 12 months, with 90% of its revenue generated outside India.

title: Practo co-founder Shashank ND’s startup Cent raises $15 Mn led by Blume, acquires Medsee
summary:
Preventive healthcare startup Cent has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. The company has also acquired AI radiology platform Medsee.
The round saw participation from individual investors Arun Sarin, Srinivas Narayanan, Sharath Narayana, Aprameya Radhakrishna and Krishan Sridhar, Cent founder Shashank ND said in a LinkedIn post.
Founded by Shashank ND, who also founded healthcare platform Practo, Cent focuses on early disease detection through medical imaging, biomarkers and artificial intelligence (AI).
Over the past year, around 10,000 people have undergone screening through Cent's protocol. Of these, one in four had a finding that required medical attention, while one in 40 needed to consult a doctor immediately, the company said.
Cent's screening protocol combines full body MRI, low dose CT scans, DEXA, ECG, ECHO and over 100 biomarkers in a single session of around two hours. The startup operates its own centres in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR, alongside its earlier network of partner diagnostic labs.
The fresh capital will be used to invest in hardware, AI and clinical research. The acquisition of Medsee will also strengthen Cent's AI capabilities, Shashank said.
Cent aims to conduct 10 million scans by 2035 and help save one million lives through early disease detection.
The startup is looking to address the gap in India's healthcare system, where several noncommunicable diseases are diagnosed at advanced stages. India has an estimated 101 million people living with diabetes and 136 million with prediabetes, while around 315 million people have hypertension, according to figures cited by Cent.
In September 2026, Practo elevated Shashank to managing director and executive chairman, while Jagnoor Singh was appointed CEO.

summary:
SVF II Ostrich (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, has sold 5.55 crore shares of Ola Electric Mobility through open market transactions between January 6 and October 22, 2026, according to Ola Electric’s regulatory filing dated October 26.
The investor also sold 1.12 crore rights entitlements during the period. Following the transactions, its shareholding in Ola Electric declined to 11.7% from 12.9%, while its holding on a diluted basis fell to 11.47% from 12.81%, as per the filing.
The stake sale comes as the Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker seeks to raise Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue. The issue opened on October 22 and will close on October 30. Ola Electric plans to issue 37.03 crore partly paid-up equity shares at Rs 27 apiece, with an upfront payment of Rs 16.20 per share.

Meanwhile, Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal pledged a 4.32% stake in the company to fund his participation in the rights issue. The pledge was created to finance his subscription, with no shares sold as part of the transaction.
The rights issue is aimed at providing additional capital to the company amid pressure on its business and financial performance. The latest fundraise follows Ola Electric's Rs 780 crore qualified institutional placement in June.

title: Luxury watch brand Rotoris raises Rs 70 Cr in Series A round led by Blume Ventures
summary:
Luxury watch brand Rotoris has raised Rs 70 crore (about $7.4 million) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from 9Unicorns, Centricity and a group of family offices, including Diwakar Goel, Atul Singh and Adhiraj Burman. Actor and television host Rannvijay Singha also participated in the round.
The company will use the fresh capital for research and development, production expansion and the growth of its physical presence in India and overseas.
Founded by Prerna Gupta and Aakash Anand, Rotoris operates an invitation only model through its Registry. The company said its first collection of 2,100 numbered watches sold out within days of its launch in February 2026. Nearly 100,000 people have since registered for access to its watches, with 40% of demand coming from markets outside India, including the US, Dubai and Australia.
In December 2025, Rotoris raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath, actor-investor Vivek Anand Oberoi, Venture Catalysts, 100 Unicorns and Tanmay Bhat. The round also saw participation from more than 30 founders, including Mamaearth's Varun Alagh, Noise's Gaurav Khatri and Snitch's Siddharth Dungarwal.
Rotoris offers collections such as Manifesta, which features natural stone dials, and Astonia, a chronograph built around a Swiss movement. Its watches are assembled and tested at the Rotoris Atelier in Gurugram, with movements sourced from Switzerland and Japan.
The company plans to expand its physical presence through Rotoris House, with plans to move beyond Delhi to Mumbai and New York.
Aakash Anand previously built and scaled beauty and personal care brand Bella Vita before exiting the business. Prerna Gupta leads Rotoris, with a focus on premium brand building and customer experience.

The proceeds will be used to expand R&D and manufacturing capacity, scale distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, and accelerate its Build Together model, Troovy said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2023 by Aditya Mukherjee and Mansi Baranwal, Troovy is a food and snacking brand that offers products such as snacks, sauces, spreads and millet pasta. The brand focuses on using carefully selected ingredients to offer convenient food options for children and families.
The company develops products based on parental inputs and insights into children's preferences. It aims to make better food choices more appealing through product innovation and a consumer-first approach.
Troovy said its vacuum-cooked potato chips contain 10% to 12% oil, compared with 35% to 40% in mainstream chips. The company also offers clean-label ketchup and seasonings for children without synthetic additives or preservatives.
The brand competes with Slurrp Farm, Timios and The Mumum Co in the kids' health food segment.
Brands such as Troovy, Slurrp Farm, Open Secret and Beyond Snack are tapping into demand for better-for-you foods while expanding across direct-to-consumer (D2C), e-commerce, quick-commerce and offline retail channels.

summary:

The proceeds will be used to build a team and develop a field ready prototype within 18 months, the company said in a press release.
Founded this year by Anish Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar, Nova Spectral AI develops lead free colloidal quantum dot (cQD) short wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chips on standard silicon CMOS for defence intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) and physical AI applications.
The Bengaluru based startup said it is developing an indigenous quantum dot SWIR image sensor chip. The technology enables cameras to capture images in conditions where conventional cameras may struggle, including low light, haze and smoke. It can be used in drones, surveillance systems, robots and autonomous vehicles.
Nova Spectral AI uses CMOS compatible manufacturing processes and indium arsenide (InAs) colloidal quantum dots to develop infrared sensors. The company aims to reduce sensor costs by up to 100 times compared with conventional indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) technology.
In defence, the technology could expand the use of SWIR imaging across drones and ISR platforms while reducing dependence on imported sensors. The company is also targeting applications in smartphones, wearables, robots and automobiles.
Colloidal quantum dot SWIR image sensors built on standard silicon CMOS are being explored as a way to make infrared imaging more affordable and scalable across applications that require vision in challenging conditions.
Another player in the space, SpectraGaze Systems, raised Rs 3.7 crore in seed funding led by GVFL to develop indigenous infrared detectors, optical imaging sensors and electro optical payloads for space and defence applications.

title: MakeMyTrip returns to profit in Q2 FY27; gross bookings grow 21%
summary:
MakeMyTrip returned to profitability in Q2 FY27 as growth in hotels, bus ticketing and ancillary services offset pressure on air travel. The Nasdaq-listed company reported a net profit of $1.8 million for the quarter ended September 2026, compared with a loss of $5.7 million a year earlier, while gross bookings rose 20.9% year-on-year in constant currency to $2.72 billion.
Revenue increased 2.5% to $235.2 million from $229.3 million, although growth stood at 11.2% after adjusting for currency movements. The Indian rupee depreciated approximately 10% against the US dollar during the quarter, affecting reported revenue growth. 
MakeMyTrip also cited elevated airfares and subdued international long-haul travel, partly offset by strong domestic demand. 
Adjusted operating profit rose to $46.2 million from $44.2 million, while adjusted net profit before tax increased 26.9% to $46.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA stood at $51.5 million, up 6.4% year-on-year. However, the return to a small reported net profit came alongside slower growth in reported revenue than in gross bookings.
Hotels and packages remained the largest contributor to adjusted margin, which rose 20.2% in constant currency to $116.8 million. Standalone hotel room nights grew 18.6%, supported by domestic hotel bookings that increased more than 20%. The company said demand for domestic leisure trips, shorter holidays and pilgrimage travel supported the segment.
Air ticketing adjusted margin increased 14.3% to $108.6 million in constant currency, despite a 7.2% decline in reported revenue from the segment to $56.7 million. Management attributed the pressure to higher fares and constrained airline capacity. It said the business maintained market share and improved unit economics through ancillary services.
Bus ticketing was another growth area. Its adjusted margin rose 29% to $45.1 million, while revenue increased 16.6% in reported terms to $19.4 million. Revenue from other businesses, including ancillary services, grew 21.6% to $21.2 million.
MakeMyTrip is also expanding its AI assistant, Myra. It handled more than 90,000 conversations daily during the quarter, resolved over 53% of post-booking flight and hotel queries, and assisted with more than 3,000 completed bookings per day. Customers using Myra completed around 1.7 times more bookings than non-users, according to the company.
Despite the quarterly turnaround, first-half net profit fell 45.8% to $10.9 million, while free cash flow declined 19.8% to $67.1 million. The figures suggest that the recovery in quarterly earnings has yet to translate into stronger year-to-date profitability.

summary:
Trading platform Mochatrade has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Zero Knowledge Ventures, among others. Its earlier backers include Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
The fresh funds will be used to develop its trading engine and risk infrastructure, as well as expand its reach among active Indian traders, Mochatrade said in a press release.
Founded this year by Utkarsh Sinha, Parth Maheshwari and Chetan Manda, Mochatrade is a trading platform for Indian users that combines UPI-based funding and rupee balances with access to contracts linked to US stocks, indices and commodities.
According to the company, users can fund their accounts through UPI and view margins, or the money set aside for trades, as well as profits and losses in rupees. Users can take long or short positions through perpetual futures contracts linked to US company prices without opening a US brokerage account. These contracts have no fixed expiry, and users do not own the underlying shares. Leverage allows users to take larger positions with less upfront capital, but also amplifies potential losses.
Through its Indian operating entity, Mochatrade is registered with the Financial Intelligence Unit India (FIU-IND) as a Virtual Digital Asset Service Provider and a reporting entity for anti-money laundering purposes.
The platform said its waitlist has crossed 25,000 sign-ups. However, it has not announced a public launch date. Users can join the waitlist on its website for early access updates.
Mochatrade also plans to introduce contracts linked to select pre-IPO companies, US stock options and social trading features, subject to applicable laws and regulatory approvals. The company said its markets are designed to offer continuous access and real-time settlement, subject to liquidity, asset availability and risk controls.

title: Snapdeal parent AceVector posts Rs 151 Cr revenue and Rs 17.6 Cr loss in Q2 FY27
summary:
AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce platform Snapdeal, has reported its first quarterly results since its listing earlier this month. The company’s revenue rose 17% year-on-year to cross Rs 150 crore in Q2 FY27, while its losses stood at Rs 17.6 crore.
According to its unaudited quarterly results, AceVector’s operating revenue stood at Rs 151.2 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 129.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Snapdeal’s marketplace business accounted for the largest share of AceVector’s operating revenue at 57%, with revenue of Rs 86.2 crore, up 15% year-on-year. Its e-commerce enablement SaaS platform, Unicommerce, contributed Rs 59 crore, while consumer brands added Rs 6 crore to operating revenue.
Including Rs 2.6 crore in non-operating income, AceVector’s total income stood at Rs 153.8 crore in Q2 FY27.
For the first half of FY27, AceVector’s consolidated revenue grew 17% year-on-year to Rs 285.5 crore, supported by growth across Snapdeal and Unicommerce. Snapdeal’s revenue rose 15% to Rs 164.4 crore, while Unicommerce recorded a 15% increase to Rs 110.4 crore.
Snapdeal’s fashion net merchandise value (NMV) rose 31% year-on-year to Rs 407.6 crore in H1 FY27. Its annual transacting customer base grew 12% to 130.8 lakh, while app-delivered units increased 23% to 133.6 lakh. During the period, the company also launched an AI solutions suite for customers, sellers and creators, with features for product discovery, personalised recommendations and seller support.
Logistics expenses remained AceVector’s largest cost at Rs 71.4 crore, up 20% year-on-year. The expense accounted for over 42% of its total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 46 crore during the quarter.
AceVector’s total expenditure rose over 21% year-on-year to Rs 168.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 138.7 crore in the year-ago quarter. The faster growth in expenses compared with revenue led to an 85% increase in losses to Rs 17.6 crore, which included Rs 1.3 crore in exceptional items.
AceVector made a weak stock market debut on the stock market, with its shares listed at an 11.5% discount to the IPO price of Rs 32. The stock opened at Rs 28.32 on the NSE and Rs 28.30 on the BSE, despite the Rs 420 crore IPO receiving around 5 times subscription. 
The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 133 crore, with a price band of Rs 30 to Rs 32 per share.
At the end of Monday’s trading session, AceVector’s shares closed at Rs 20.92, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,138 crore.
